## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Only diagnosis code is supplied; the underlying architecture and final user-representation computation cannot be verified. The compatibility view exposes `item_emb.weight`, `log2feats(sequence)` returning B × L × D position features, and `predict_score(features, items)`. Diagnosis uses features at valid sequence positions rather than explicitly selecting a final user vector.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` retains the compatibility view and verifies that `view.model` is the actual trained `nn.Module`. It also stores metadata, review data and training histories, but these probes do not use them.

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` copies at most ten batches to CPU. Each batch must contain `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with matching B × L tensors. Probes run without gradients in evaluation mode; module modes and global Python, NumPy, PyTorch and initialized CUDA random states are restored afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding cosine:** Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding item embeddings with seed 42, computes mean off-diagonal cosine, and maps it to [0,1]. A value of 0.5 means average cosine zero; higher values indicate alignment, without establishing collapse or recommendation diversity.
- **Positive–negative margins:** Scores supplied positive and negative items at nonpadding positions with distinct, nonzero IDs. Reports mean margin, nearest-rank 10th percentile, negative-beats-positive rate and fraction below 0.5. Larger margins and fewer ranking errors generally indicate stronger sampled training separation, but margins depend on score scale and negative sampling.
- **Coverage:** Reports observed, finite and nonfinite margin positions. Nonfinite values indicate numerical problems and are excluded from summaries.

# Perturbation & Tests

Causal consistency uses the first two batches, capped at eight sequences each. At selected observed-event boundaries, future items become padding while absolute positions remain fixed. Earlier features are compared against their originals. Zero violations within coordinate tolerances supports sampled causal consistency; positive violations reveal future dependence or numerical sensitivity. Counts and maximum absolute error accompany the violation rate.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The result contains `metrics` and matching `metric_definitions`. Metric families cover embedding cosine, training margins, coverage and causal consistency. Unavailable measurements return `None`; category breakdown explicitly reports `available: false`.

These probes do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, semantic relevance, simulator traits or recommendation diversity. Categories and review content are unavailable.  ## Search results
Research supports testing diagnostic correctness before trusting quality claims. A [2024 recommender metamorphic-testing study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950584924000156) evaluates reliability through expected relationships between executions. Applied here, useful proposed mutations include disabled branches, shuffled titles/descriptions, corrupted attention masks, and mismatched checkpoint exports. Each probe should detect its relevant fault while accepting valid transformations; unused text should have no effect. Positive score rescaling must preserve ranking metrics for fixed candidates and consistent tie handling, although losses and margins may change. These are proposed checks, not evidence that this toolkit already detects failures.

Sampled ranking requires particular caution. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show that sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; small candidate sets also blur distinctions between metrics. [RecSys 2025 research](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) examines sampling reliability, while [RecSys 2026 work](https://mdw.ekstrandom.net/pubs/recsys26-eval) studies agreement between evaluation designs and dense relevance judgments. Consequently, HR@10 against 99 negatives and full-catalog recommendation measure different tasks; diagnostic sensitivity to candidate count, sampling distribution, and seed deserves explicit measurement.

For this benchmark, retain pinned host macro validation HR@10 as the selection criterion. Within the shared budget, compare diagnostic changes with host-exposed validation changes across all four datasets, reporting per-category results alongside the macro average. Use training-prefix audits only as auxiliary measurements because fitted histories can overstate generalization. Check exported-predictor score and ranking agreement directly. Mutation detection establishes fault sensitivity; improved training margins or embedding alignment alone does not establish recommendation quality.

Recent work supports separating preference polarity from factual support. [Disentangling Likes and Dislikes (2024; revised 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13248) evaluates whether recommendation explanations align with user sentiment, beyond textual similarity. [GenAudit (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12566) links supported claims to reference evidence and revises unsupported claims; [QASemConsistency (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07473) decomposes text into minimal propositions, reporting annotation agreement κ>0.7. These suggest auditing each feedback reason separately, with exact source spans, rather than judging an entire explanation at once.

Proposed adaptation: record user/item IDs, selected/rejected status, original rank, verbatim feedback, reason category, title/description offsets, and evidence status: supported, contradicted, or insufficient information. Categories can include feature match, explicit specification conflict, redundancy, and missing information. Compatibility conflicts require both an explicit requirement and a conflicting specification; absent specifications mean insufficient information. Interaction history alone establishes neither ownership nor satisfaction. Ownership, unmet needs, and diversity/conformity traits remain unknown without direct evidence. Double-annotate cases independently; report raw agreement, Cohen’s κ for reason/evidence labels, span-overlap F1, and adjudicated disagreements. This is a proposed protocol, not an established recommendation taxonomy.

For the twenty users, report case-level selected–rejected rank inversions: among explicitly compared pairs, count cases where a selected item originally ranked below a rejected item, with ties and unranked items separate. Keep these diagnostics separate from macro validation HR@10. A [2026 study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijhcs.2025.103720) found persuasive explanations can shift choices toward lower-utility options, reinforcing that selection does not establish factual correctness. Treat this small sample as case analysis, without population-level preference estimates.

Recent work supports diagnosing history dependence through prediction changes. [Measuring Recency Bias (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) proposes a recency metric and reports that excessive recent-item emphasis harms accuracy across its evaluated models. [TRACE (RecSys 2026)](https://github.com/devUuung/TRACE) uses influence-guided position selection, plausible substitutions and actual ranking margins to find history edits that promote or demote target items. A [2026 temporal-attribution study](https://jidmis.org/index.php/jidmis/article/view/2525) evaluates perturbation explanations through faithfulness, robustness, k-sufficiency and mask-versus-shuffle consistency. These approaches motivate measuring both score margins and ranking changes, rather than interpreting attention weights alone.

# Probes & Metrics

Reports mean margin, nearest-rank 10th percentile, negative-beats-positive rate and fraction below 0.5. Larger margins and fewer ranking errors generally indicate stronger sampled training separation, but margins depend on score scale and negative sampling.
- **Coverage:** Reports observed, finite and nonfinite margin positions. Nonfinite values indicate numerical problems and are excluded from summaries.

Earlier features are compared against their originals. Zero violations within coordinate tolerances supports sampled causal consistency; positive violations reveal future dependence or numerical sensitivity. Counts and maximum absolute error accompany the violation rate.
